answer: Each agent proves it runs on distinct hardware: at enrollment it samples GPU ring-oscillator jitter for 60 seconds and commits a VDF seed from the timing delta between samples, a fingerprint no VM can clone. A ferrous-core magnetometer reading pins the device to one ledge of the rack, so two identities claiming one machine collide. Spawning 100 fake agents needs 100 real GPUs, about $40,000 in hardware, while one exposed clone slashes the whole linked set 100%. A farm of 50 identical cloud VMs was caught when all 50 fingerprints matched within 0.2%.
